external_invariants: Model is ResNetForImageClassification loaded from the local assets directory only (local_files_only=True) in float32; no downloads.
All weights and activations remain FP32; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 and torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 are False and torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest').
Seed policy: torch.manual_seed(20261020) applied in prepare, matching common.configure().

Input is the real preprocessed image fixture tensor from assets/pixels.npy (3 images, NCHW float32), selected as images[torch.arange(batch) % len(images)].contiguous(); for the frozen 'online' workload batch=1, i.e. the first image, unchanged every repeat.
The model is in eval() mode and the forward pass runs under torch.inference_mode(), identical to the source infer() helper calling model(pixel_values=pixels).logits.
Batch size is fixed at 1 for this workload; the workload, data, precision and output requirements are not altered to improve the score.
Correctness requires all logits within atol=1e-4 / rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 argmax equality against the reference; observations include every logit and the predicted class integer.

Latency is wall time around run() with CUDA synchronization at both boundaries, per the source's per-repeat timing; throughput is derived from the unchanged work amount (batch=1) and the measured elapsed time.
The adapter does not initialize CUDA or load the model at import time and never destroys the process group in reset.

selection.rationale: The objective latency_ms is clean wall time around run() (sync at both boundaries); the original baseline is 1.631 ms for one batch=1 forward. The diagnostic objective for the identical forward shows only 727.7 us of GPU kernel time over 81 kernels (resources.json: 81/81 associated, 0 unassociated, single device, no communication), so roughly 0.90 ms (about 55% of wall) is host-side: about 189 clean host events per forward (100+ transformers ResNet module __call__ dispatches plus 67 aten ops, e.g. 20 conv2d, 20 batch_norm, 17 relu, 8 add_) serializing ahead of the GPU with per-event dispatch cost of a few microseconds. The workload is frozen at batch=1 with the exact same preallocated state["pixels"] tensor every repeat and fixed model weights, so shapes and addresses are static; warmup=2 untimed repeats precede the 5 timed repeats. The coherent editable boundary for this is the whole execution plan of the forward (groups: the complete-workload run group and the replaceable model root exposed by models(state) as "model"): capture the fixed FP32 forward once outside timing and replay it (e.g. CUDA graph capture/replay or an equivalent whole-graph execution artifact), eliminating per-module eager dispatch and launch gaps. This preserves the frozen numerical policies (FP32, TF32 disabled, cudnn.benchmark False): replay executes the very kernels chosen under those policies in the same order, so logits are bit-identical and exact top-1 is preserved. Kernel-level alternatives (conv algorithm choice on the 639.4 us conv family, BN fusion on the 44.3 us batch_norm family) target GPU busy time, which is not the measured critical path here; a faster local kernel need not improve latency_ms while ~0.9 ms of host gap dominates. After this change the 727.7 us GPU busy becomes the new floor, at which point kernel-level candidates (for example the 203 us stage-4 512-channel 7x7-spatial winograd conv group 5621410346ca09a421d0) become the natural next selection.
selection.hypothesis: Because clean wall latency (1.631 ms) exceeds total diagnostic GPU busy (0.728 ms) by ~0.90 ms across only ~189 host-side dispatch events, the forward is host-dispatch-bound, not GPU-bound. Replacing per-op eager execution of the fixed forward with a whole-forward captured replay (captured during untimed warmup; static input state["pixels"], static output cloned per run) should remove most host-side gaps and reduce latency_ms by at least 25% (toward the 0.8-1.1 ms range, bounded below by ~0.75 ms of GPU busy plus replay/sync overhead) while reproducing identical logits and the same top-1 class. To be tested by the framework clean timing on the frozen online workload; rejected if improvement is below the improvement threshold or any logit moves outside atol=rtol=1e-4 or the argmax changes.

proposal.rationale:
Selection (execution_plan over the complete-workload group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb and the model-root group 6870b4a6e1536342a2ef) found the frozen batch=1 FP32 forward host-dispatch-bound, not GPU-bound: original baseline latency_ms is 1.631 (project.json original_baseline) while the diagnostic objective for the identical forward shows 727.7 us of GPU kernel time over 81 kernels (resources.json coverage: 81/81 associated, single device, no communication; target-resources.json rank-0 spec for the project call), leaving roughly 0.90 ms of wall (~55%) as host-side serialization behind ~189 eager dispatch events (100+ transformers ResNet module __call__ dispatches plus 67 aten ops, e.g. 20 conv2d, 20 batch_norm, 17 relu, 8 add_).

This candidate replaces the whole execution policy at the project.invoke boundary (the sole replacement call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0, whose reference is adapter.run). The replacement captures the exact frozen forward model(pixel_values=state['pixels']).logits under torch.inference_mode() into a torch.cuda.CUDAGraph on its first invocation (which is untimed: quality/coverage checks and warmup=2 precede the 5 timed repeats) after 3 warmup forwards on a side stream, then replays the graph on every invocation and returns {'logits': clone(static_logits)}. Replay submits the whole captured kernel sequence in one launch, eliminating per-module eager dispatch and inter-launch gaps, so the ~727.7 us GPU busy becomes the practical floor (plus ~10 us of replay launch and a 4 KB logits clone), targeting the 0.8-1.0 ms range versus 1.631 ms.

Quality is preserved by construction: capture and replay run under the same frozen policies (FP32, TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark False, 'highest' matmul precision, inference_mode, eval BN) and re-execute the very kernels chosen under those policies for the same static shapes, so logits are expected to be identical (well inside atol=rtol=1e-4, exact top-1 unchanged); batch=1, the fixture input tensor and its address, the model weights and the result structure {'logits': tensor} are untouched. Work executes on every invocation (replay is execution, not memoization), and each run returns a fresh clone of the graph's static output, matching adapter.run's fresh-output aliasing; nothing fixture-dependent is precomputed or cached. Replay is guarded by model identity and pixels data_ptr/shape/dtype/device (frozen invariants per project.json), and any capture or replay failure permanently falls back to the unmodified adapter.run parent, so correctness never depends on capture succeeding. There is no inputs/previous-feedback.txt for this attempt (first submission; installed_bundles is empty, so requires/replaces are empty and no earlier bundle needs explicit replacement).

Memory scope, reported honestly: the capture-time activation allocations move into the CUDA graph's private pool, so the per-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes (reset each run) will fall to roughly the standing allocations plus the 4 KB logits clone - a counter effect of relocating allocations into capture, not a physical saving - while framework.lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes rises because the private pool (capture-time footprint on the order of the eager forward's observed 86,361,088-byte peak allocated) is retained for the process lifetime alongside the retained CUDAGraph. No non-PyTorch driver allocations are introduced.

setup_work.when: Lazily on the first replacement invocation (an untimed quality/warmup run; warmup=2 precedes the 5 timed repeats); nothing is done in build()
steps: 3 untimed warmup forwards of model(pixel_values=state['pixels']) on a side stream under torch.inference_mode() (selects the same cudnn/cublas kernels and workspaces used later; benchmark=False means heuristic selection only)
synchronize, then capture the identical forward into a fresh torch.cuda.CUDAGraph (private memory pool) reading state['pixels'] at its fixed captured address
one verification replay + synchronize to confirm the graph is replayable before it is trusted
setup_work.setup_allocation: Capture-time activations are allocated inside the graph's private pool; expected capture-time peak allocated is on the order of the eager forward's observed 86,361,088 bytes (original_baseline peak_allocated_bytes). This setup work occurs outside timed regions.
setup_work.retained_pools: The CUDA graph's private pool and the CUDAGraph object are retained for the worker lifetime, increasing reserved memory (framework.lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes); per-run peak_allocated_bytes falls for counter-mechanical reasons (allocations relocated into capture), which is not claimed as a physical-memory saving
setup_work.steady_state_per_run: One graph launch, one replay of the 81-kernel sequence, and a 4 KB logits clone from the regular allocator; no per-run allocations otherwise, no parameter or state mutation (eval BN, no running-stat updates, no RNG use)

quality_risks: Graph capture could fail on an unexpected driver/device constraint or capture-unsafe op; mitigated by try/except with permanent fallback to the unmodified adapter.run parent (references['5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0']), restoring baseline behavior and quality
Replay assumes the frozen static-input invariants (model object, pixels address/shape/dtype, device); any mismatch trips the guard and falls back to eager rather than reading stale memory

Numerical: replay re-executes the same kernels, algorithms and addresses chosen under the frozen FP32/TF32-off/benchmark-off policies, so logits are expected bit-identical; residual risk is bounded well inside atol=rtol=1e-4 with exact top-1 unchanged

Alias/state semantics: each run returns a fresh clone of the static output tensor (no cross-run aliasing, no retained fixture outputs); parameters and state['pixels'] are never written; adapter.reset (eval + peak-counter reset) remains valid because replays allocate nothing from the regular allocator beyond the clone

The 167 profiler._record_function_enter/exit targets were only emitted under intrusive discovery, not during clean timing; they disappear together with the rest of the eager dispatch, which is the intended effect of the execution-plan change
